status: Fresh-workload exploratory follow-up, designed after the initial list-theory diagnostic; not externally preregistered
hypothesis: Finite counterexample screening dominates acquisition cost. Since the proof checker alone establishes validity, using eight predetermined screening assignments may reduce total acquisition cost without reducing formally checked held-out performance. This optimization must also be given to ordinary full completion, so any gain cannot be attributed uniquely to failure-guided discovery.
unchanged: Same four list definitions, checker, candidate term grammar (five nodes), proof search, training target, and full-completion stopping rules as frozen v3
workload: 100 new positive equations: random terms with exactly 9 through 23 AST nodes, containing reverse and at least two original list variables, compared with a canonical concatenation/reversal expression. 20 false controls replace one original variable in a positive normal form with a fresh W. A concrete length counterexample is checked for each false control. Final order is shuffled deterministically. Terms are generated and frozen before these methods run; no initial held-out equation is reused.
success: Accepted separate-kernel certificate; every accepted bundle is replayed. False controls must have no accepted certificate. All acquisition and test search costs use the same accounting; CPU/wall measured separately.
interpretation: At most evidence for a conventional screening optimization. No claim of new mathematics, a learned language, new semantics, or a distinctive categorical mechanism. Any improvement must be reported for the optimized strongest ordinary baseline as well. No adjustment of sample size, seed, or workload after observing results.
